answer.evidence: The car is drawn as a vehicle side view, so it is only loosely a box. The roof is a large lighter red band at rows 6-15, with a highlight and a darker edge line at row 16. Dark eave-shadow rows 17-18 follow, then the window band (rows 19-24) and the door/body face (rows 25-37), with wheels down to row 44. The roof reads as a sloped top plane above an edge line, and the side body is the south face. The yellow headlight on the right means it faces east. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The red car body is built from roughly 3 red steps (a light highlight strip, a mid red, a dark lower shade) plus a dark outline. The references use about 5-6 steps per material. The measured facts back this up: 89% of the candidate's dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a uniform near-black line that gives a sticker look. The references with tinted outlines (hedge 0%, cheese stall 1%) lean toward the material tone. The wheels and windows are dark, near-neutral fills. The large door and side panels are smooth, flat red with no grain, dots or paint variation, and 15% of the candidate is near-flat. That is similar to the cheese stall (13%), but the stall has visible texture elsewhere. Visible tones per tile (8) are far below the well (20) and stall (17) and only comparable to the hedge (9), so the candidate is thinner and flatter than the richer references. A careful artist would not accept it next to the well and stall.

styleAnswer.evidence: The red car body has about 3 lightness steps (highlight, mid red, dark red) and little grain. The doors, hood and roof are smooth panels with only a single highlight streak, and the windows are flat dark blue with a small glint. The outline is a dark near-neutral line around the whole car and wheels, and 89% of the dark edge pixels are neutral. That is the sticker look, against the dark-material-tone edges of the stall (1% neutral) and the hedge (0%). The measured 8 visible tones per tile is below the stall (17) and the well (20), and the car is a large object that should carry that much detail. Its 15% near-flat coverage is above the hedge, well and bench (0%). The result is a clean but shallow, flat vector-like car and not the layered, textured Beodeul standard.
